**[SECTION 3: STUDY OBJECTIVES AND ENDPOINTS]{.underline}**

**[3.1 Primary Objective]{.underline}**

The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of PTX-4820 compared with placebo in improving liver fibrosis in adults with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) and liver fibrosis stage F2 or F3 (NASH CRN classification) after 52 weeks of treatment. This objective will be assessed through centralized histological evaluation of paired liver biopsy specimens obtained at baseline and at Week 52.

**[3.2 Secondary Objectives]{.underline}**

The secondary objectives of this study are:

> 1\. To evaluate the dose-response relationship of PTX-4820 across three dose levels (5 mg, 15 mg, and 30 mg administered subcutaneously once weekly) with respect to the primary efficacy endpoint and key secondary efficacy endpoints.
>
> 2\. To assess the effect of PTX-4820 on histological resolution of NASH without worsening of liver fibrosis at Week 52.
>
> 3\. To evaluate changes in liver enzymes (ALT and AST), liver stiffness (as measured by FibroScan transient elastography), and body weight from baseline to Week 52 across treatment arms.
>
> 4\. To characterize the pharmacokinetic (PK) profile of PTX-4820 at each dose level, including estimation of key PK parameters at steady state.
>
> 5\. To evaluate the overall safety and tolerability of PTX-4820 at each dose level over 52 weeks of treatment and 12 weeks of post-treatment follow-up, including assessment of adverse events, serious adverse events, clinical laboratory parameters, vital signs, and electrocardiographic parameters.

**[3.3 Exploratory Objectives]{.underline}**

The exploratory objectives of this study are:

> 1\. To evaluate changes in non-invasive biomarkers of liver fibrosis and inflammation, including the Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) score, Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4), and AST to Platelet Ratio Index (APRI), from baseline to Week 52.
>
> 2\. To explore the relationship between PNPLA3 genotype (rs738409 polymorphism) and treatment response to PTX-4820.
>
> 3\. To evaluate patient-reported outcomes, including disease-specific quality of life and gastrointestinal symptom assessments, during the treatment period.
>
> 4\. To assess changes in hepatic steatosis as measured by magnetic resonance imaging--proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) in a subset of subjects at selected sites.

**[3.4 Endpoints]{.underline}**

**3.4.1 Primary Endpoint**

The primary efficacy endpoint is the proportion of subjects achieving ≥1-stage improvement in liver fibrosis (NASH CRN scoring system) with no worsening of NASH (defined as no increase in NAS for ballooning, inflammation, or steatosis components) at Week 52, assessed by paired liver biopsy (baseline and Week 52). Liver biopsy specimens will be centrally read using the NASH CRN histological scoring system.

**3.4.2 Key Secondary Endpoints**

The key secondary efficacy endpoints, listed in hierarchical order for multiplicity adjustment, are:

> 1\. Proportion of subjects achieving NASH resolution (defined as a hepatocyte ballooning score of 0 and a lobular inflammation score of 0 or 1) without worsening of fibrosis (no increase in fibrosis stage) at Week 52.
>
> 2\. Proportion of subjects achieving ≥2-point reduction in NAFLD Activity Score (NAS) at Week 52.
>
> 3\. Change from baseline to Week 52 in serum ALT and AST levels.
>
> 4\. Change from baseline to Week 52 in liver stiffness as measured by FibroScan (transient elastography), expressed in kilopascals (kPa).
>
> 5\. Change from baseline in body weight (absolute change in kilograms and percentage change from baseline) at Week 52.
>
> 6\. Pharmacokinetic parameters at steady state: maximum observed plasma concentration (Cmax), area under the concentration-time curve over the dosing interval (AUC0-tau), and trough plasma concentration (Ctrough).

**3.4.3 Safety Endpoints**

Safety endpoints include:

> • Incidence, severity, and relationship to study drug of all adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs)
>
> • Incidence of adverse events of special interest (AESIs)
>
> • Incidence of AEs leading to study drug discontinuation
>
> • Changes from baseline in vital signs, 12-lead ECG parameters (including QTcF interval), and clinical laboratory parameters
>
> • Incidence of clinically significant laboratory abnormalities

**[SECTION 4: STUDY POPULATION]{.underline}**

**[4.1 Inclusion Criteria]{.underline}**

Subjects must meet ALL of the following criteria to be eligible for enrollment in this study:

> 1\. Adults aged 18 to 75 years, inclusive, at the time of informed consent.
>
> 2\. Histologically confirmed NASH on a liver biopsy obtained within 6 months prior to the Screening visit (or performed during the Screening period), with a NAFLD Activity Score (NAS) ≥4, including at least 1 point each for steatosis, at least 1 point for lobular inflammation, and at least 1 point for hepatocyte ballooning.
>
> 3\. Liver fibrosis stage F2 or F3 on the qualifying liver biopsy, as determined by the NASH CRN classification system.
>
> 4\. Body mass index (BMI) ≥25 kg/m² at the Screening visit.
>
> 5\. Stable body weight, defined as no more than ±5% change in body weight, for at least 3 months prior to the Screening visit, as confirmed by medical records or subject self-report.
>
> 6\. Willing and able to undergo a percutaneous liver biopsy at baseline (if a qualifying biopsy obtained during screening does not serve as the baseline biopsy per protocol) and at Week 52.
>
> 7\. Able to provide written informed consent and willing to comply with all study procedures, visit schedules, and requirements as described in this protocol.
>
> 8\. Willing and able to self-administer weekly subcutaneous injections of study drug (or have a designated caregiver administer injections) following appropriate training by site staff.

**[4.2 Exclusion Criteria]{.underline}**

Subjects meeting ANY of the following criteria will be excluded from participation:

> 1\. Evidence of cirrhosis (fibrosis stage F4) on the qualifying liver biopsy.
>
> 2\. History of hepatic decompensation, including variceal bleeding, ascites requiring diuretic therapy or paracentesis, or hepatic encephalopathy.
>
> 3\. Known or suspected chronic liver disease of any etiology other than NASH, including but not limited to: alcoholic liver disease, chronic hepatitis B virus infection (hepatitis B surface antigen positive), chronic hepatitis C virus infection (hepatitis C antibody positive with detectable HCV RNA), autoimmune hepatitis, Wilson\'s disease, hemochromatosis, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, primary biliary cholangitis, or primary sclerosing cholangitis.
>
> 4\. Current daily alcohol consumption exceeding 30 grams per day for men or 20 grams per day for women, or a pattern of binge drinking, within the 12 months prior to the Screening visit, as assessed by investigator interview and the AUDIT-C questionnaire.
>
> 5\. History of bariatric surgery (including but not limited to Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, sleeve gastrectomy, adjustable gastric banding, or biliopancreatic diversion) within 5 years prior to the Screening visit.
>
> 6\. Use of medications known to cause hepatic steatosis or steatohepatitis (e.g., amiodarone, methotrexate, tamoxifen, systemic corticosteroids at doses equivalent to ≥10 mg/day of prednisone for more than 2 consecutive weeks) within 6 months prior to the Screening visit.
>
> 7\. Type 1 diabetes mellitus.
>
> 8\. Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) \>10.0% at the Screening visit.
>
> 9\. Uncontrolled hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure \>160 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure \>100 mmHg at the Screening visit despite antihypertensive therapy.
>
> 10\. Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).
>
> 11\. History of acute or chronic pancreatitis.
>
> 12\. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) \<30 mL/min/1.73 m² at the Screening visit, as calculated by the CKD-EPI equation.
>
> 13\. Known hypersensitivity or contraindication to GLP-1 receptor agonists or any component of the study drug formulation.
>
> 14\. Participation in another interventional clinical trial with receipt of an investigational product within 30 days or 5 half-lives of the investigational product (whichever is longer) prior to the Screening visit.
>
> 15\. Any other medical condition, psychiatric illness, social circumstance, or laboratory abnormality that, in the opinion of the investigator, would jeopardize the safety of the subject, interfere with the subject\'s ability to comply with protocol requirements, or compromise the integrity of the study data.

**[4.3 Withdrawal Criteria and Subject Discontinuation]{.underline}**

A subject may voluntarily withdraw from the study at any time for any reason, without prejudice to future medical care. The investigator should make reasonable efforts to ascertain the reason for withdrawal, but the subject is not obligated to provide a reason.

The investigator may withdraw a subject from the study for any of the following reasons:

> • Safety concerns, including the occurrence of an adverse event that, in the investigator\'s judgment, makes continued participation potentially harmful to the subject
>
> • Significant non-compliance with study procedures, visit schedule, or study drug administration
>
> • Subject is lost to follow-up despite reasonable attempts to contact the subject (a minimum of 3 documented contact attempts by different methods)
>
> • The subject becomes pregnant (see Section 9.5, Stopping Rules)
>
> • Development of any condition that meets the exclusion criteria during the course of the study
>
> • Investigator judgment that withdrawal is in the best interest of the subject

Subjects who discontinue study drug for any reason will be strongly encouraged to remain in the study for all scheduled safety follow-up assessments through the end-of-study visit (Week 64). The Week 52 liver biopsy should still be performed, if the subject consents, to allow evaluation of treatment effects. All subjects who receive at least one dose of study drug will be included in the safety analysis regardless of the duration of treatment.

The reason for discontinuation of study drug and/or withdrawal from the study will be documented in the subject\'s source documents and the electronic case report form (eCRF).

**[SECTION 5: STUDY DESIGN AND TREATMENT]{.underline}**

**[5.1 Overall Study Design]{.underline}**

This is a Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, dose-ranging study of PTX-4820 in adults with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) and liver fibrosis stage F2 or F3. The study will be conducted at approximately 28 clinical sites (22 in the United States and 6 in Canada).

Eligible subjects will be randomized in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to one of four treatment arms:

> • **Arm A:** PTX-4820 5 mg subcutaneous (SC) weekly
>
> • **Arm B:** PTX-4820 15 mg SC weekly
>
> • **Arm C:** PTX-4820 30 mg SC weekly
>
> • **Arm D:** Matching placebo SC weekly

Randomization will be stratified by two factors: (1) liver fibrosis stage at baseline (F2 vs. F3) and (2) presence of type 2 diabetes mellitus at baseline (yes vs. no). Randomization will be performed centrally using an Interactive Response Technology (IRT) system.

The study consists of four periods:

> • **Screening Period:** Up to 8 weeks (56 days) prior to the Baseline/Randomization visit (Day 1). This period allows for the collection of screening assessments, confirmation of eligibility, and obtaining the qualifying liver biopsy (if not already available).
>
> • **Treatment Period:** 52 weeks (Day 1 through Week 52). Subjects will self-administer weekly SC injections of study drug. The first dose will be administered at the study site under the supervision of trained site staff. Subsequent doses will be self-administered at home.
>
> • **Post-Treatment Follow-Up Period:** 12 weeks (Week 52 through Week 64). Subjects will return for follow-up visits at Weeks 56, 60, and 64 after completing the treatment period.
>
> • **Total duration of subject participation:** Approximately 72 weeks from the initiation of screening through the end-of-study visit, or approximately 64 weeks from randomization through the end of follow-up.

**Figure 1: Study Schema**

Screening (up to 8 weeks) → Randomization (Day 1) → Treatment Period (52 weeks) → Post-Treatment Follow-Up (12 weeks, through Week 64)

At randomization, subjects are assigned 1:1:1:1 to: Arm A (5 mg), Arm B (15 mg), Arm C (30 mg), or Arm D (Placebo). Liver biopsies are performed at Baseline and Week 52. FibroScan assessments occur at Screening, Week 24, and Week 52.

**[5.2 Dosing and Dose Escalation]{.underline}**

The dosing regimen for each treatment arm, including dose titration schedules where applicable, is described below and summarized in Table 3.

**Table 3: Dose Titration Schedule**

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Week**        **Arm A (5 mg)**   **Arm B (15 mg)**   **Arm C (30 mg)**   **Arm D (Placebo)**
  --------------- ------------------ ------------------- ------------------- ---------------------
  Week 1          5 mg               5 mg                5 mg                Placebo

  Week 2          5 mg               15 mg               15 mg               Placebo

  Week 3 onward   5 mg               15 mg               30 mg               Placebo
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Arm A (PTX-4820 5 mg):** Subjects randomized to Arm A will receive PTX-4820 5 mg SC once weekly beginning on Day 1. No dose titration is required; the full 5 mg dose will be administered from Day 1 through Week 52.

**Arm B (PTX-4820 15 mg):** Subjects randomized to Arm B will receive PTX-4820 5 mg SC once weekly during Week 1, followed by 15 mg SC once weekly from Week 2 through Week 52. This 1-week titration is intended to improve gastrointestinal tolerability during treatment initiation.

**Arm C (PTX-4820 30 mg):** Subjects randomized to Arm C will receive PTX-4820 5 mg SC once weekly during Week 1, followed by PTX-4820 15 mg SC once weekly during Week 2, followed by PTX-4820 30 mg SC once weekly from Week 3 through Week 52. This 2-week titration schedule allows subjects to reach the full 30 mg target dose by Week 3.

**Arm D (Placebo):** Subjects randomized to Arm D will receive matching placebo SC once weekly from Day 1 through Week 52.

**Administration:** Study drug will be administered as a subcutaneous injection. The first dose (Day 1) will be administered at the study site under the supervision of trained site staff, who will provide instruction on proper self-injection technique. Subjects will demonstrate competency in self-injection before being allowed to administer subsequent doses at home. Study drug should be administered once weekly, with a dosing window of ±2 days permitted.

**Injection Sites:** Recommended injection sites include the abdomen (avoiding the 2-inch area around the navel), the front of the thigh, or the upper arm. Subjects should rotate injection sites with each dose.

Study drug supply will be managed by Kensington Drug Supply Services (Kensington, NJ), which will be responsible for packaging, labeling, and distribution of study drug to clinical sites via the IRT system.

**[5.3 Blinding]{.underline}**

This study is double-blinded. Subjects, investigators, site staff, the Sponsor study team, and the Trident CRO study team will be blinded to individual treatment assignments throughout the study. Matching placebo will be provided in prefilled syringes that are identical in appearance to the active study drug syringes. The prefilled syringes for all dose strengths and placebo will be visually indistinguishable, and the labeling will not reveal the contents.

Randomization codes will be generated and securely maintained by the IRT vendor (Meridian IRT Solutions, Philadelphia, PA). Treatment assignments will be stored within the IRT system and accessible only to authorized unblinded personnel in the event of an emergency.

**Emergency Unblinding:** In the event of a medical emergency where knowledge of the subject\'s treatment assignment is essential for proper medical management, the investigator may unblind the subject\'s treatment assignment via the IRT system, which is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The investigator should make every reasonable effort to contact the Sponsor\'s Medical Monitor (Dr. Rajiv Anand) before unblinding and must document the reason for unblinding. Unblinding for regulatory safety reporting purposes will be handled by the Sponsor\'s designated unblinded safety team and will not affect the blinding of the investigator or site staff.

**[5.4 Concomitant Medications]{.underline}**

**Permitted Medications:** The following medications are permitted during the study, provided they are administered at stable doses:

> • Metformin for type 2 diabetes, if on a stable dose for ≥3 months prior to screening
>
> • Sulfonylureas, DPP-4 inhibitors, or SGLT2 inhibitors for type 2 diabetes, if on a stable dose for ≥3 months prior to screening
>
> • Insulin therapy at a stable dose (±10% total daily dose) for ≥3 months prior to screening
>
> • Statins or other lipid-lowering agents, if on a stable dose for ≥3 months prior to screening
>
> • Antihypertensive medications at stable doses
>
> • Vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol), if on a stable dose of ≤800 IU/day for ≥6 months prior to screening

**Prohibited Medications:** The following medications are prohibited during the study:

> • GLP-1 receptor agonists (other than the study drug) or GIP receptor agonists
>
> • Obeticholic acid, elafibranor, or other investigational agents being developed for NASH treatment
>
> • Prescription or over-the-counter weight loss medications (e.g., orlistat, phentermine, lorcaserin)
>
> • Systemic corticosteroids (except short courses of ≤7 days for acute conditions unrelated to the study)
>
> • Medications known to cause hepatic steatosis (e.g., amiodarone, methotrexate, tamoxifen)

Subjects on stable background therapy for type 2 diabetes mellitus at screening must remain on stable doses of their antidiabetic medications throughout the treatment period, with dose adjustments permitted only for safety reasons (e.g., hypoglycemia management). Any changes in concomitant medications must be documented in the eCRF.

**[5.5 Study Drug Supply and Accountability]{.underline}**

PTX-4820 will be supplied as prefilled, single-use syringes at three concentrations: 5 mg/0.5 mL, 15 mg/0.5 mL, and 30 mg/0.5 mL. Matching placebo will be supplied in identical prefilled, single-use syringes containing the formulation vehicle without the active ingredient.

Study drug must be stored under refrigerated conditions at 2--8°C (36--46°F) and protected from light. Study drug must not be frozen. Study drug removed from refrigerated storage must be used within 30 minutes and may not be returned to refrigerated storage.

Drug packaging, labeling, and distribution to clinical sites will be managed by Kensington Drug Supply Services. Study drug will be shipped to sites in temperature-controlled containers with validated cold-chain packaging. Upon receipt at the site, study drug must be inventoried and stored in a secure, temperature-monitored refrigerator accessible only to authorized study personnel.

Drug accountability will be maintained by site personnel using drug accountability logs. At each monitoring visit, the clinical monitor (CRA) will verify drug accountability records against pharmacy dispensing records and returned/unused drug supplies. Unused or expired study drug will be destroyed according to the Sponsor\'s instructions or returned to the Sponsor, as specified in the Pharmacy Manual.

**[6.2 Screening Procedures]{.underline}**

The Screening period begins with the signing of the informed consent form (ICF) and may extend for up to 8 weeks (56 days) prior to the Baseline/Randomization visit (Day 1). All screening assessments must be completed and eligibility confirmed prior to randomization. The following procedures will be performed during the Screening period:

Written informed consent will be obtained from each prospective subject prior to the performance of any study-specific procedures. The informed consent process will be conducted in accordance with 21 CFR Part 50 and ICH E6(R2), as described in Section 11.1.

A comprehensive medical history will be obtained, including history of liver disease, metabolic conditions (diabetes, obesity, dyslipidemia), cardiovascular disease, gastrointestinal disorders, malignancies, surgical history, and family history with particular attention to thyroid cancer and MEN 2 syndrome. A complete list of current and recent medications will be recorded.

The qualifying liver biopsy specimen will be reviewed to confirm the diagnosis of NASH with fibrosis stage F2 or F3. If the subject has a qualifying liver biopsy obtained within 6 months prior to the Screening visit, that biopsy may serve as the qualifying biopsy. If no qualifying biopsy is available or the existing biopsy is older than 6 months, a new liver biopsy will be performed during the Screening period.

A complete physical examination will be performed, including a targeted hepatic and abdominal examination. Vital signs (systolic and diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, and oral temperature) will be recorded. Height, weight, and BMI will be measured and calculated. A 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) will be performed.

Laboratory assessments will include: complete blood count (CBC) with differential; comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) including liver function tests (ALT, AST, ALP, total bilirubin, direct bilirubin, albumin), electrolytes, BUN, creatinine, glucose; INR; lipid panel (total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides); HbA1c; fasting glucose and fasting insulin; urinalysis; amylase and lipase; and thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4).

Screening serological and etiological testing will include: hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C antibody, antinuclear antibody (ANA), anti-smooth muscle antibody (anti-SMA), ceruloplasmin, and alpha-1 antitrypsin level.

FibroScan (transient elastography) will be performed at a designated time during the screening period to obtain a baseline measurement of liver stiffness.

Assessment of all inclusion and exclusion criteria will be completed during the Screening period. Subjects who do not meet all eligibility criteria may be rescreened once with Sponsor approval.

**[6.3 Baseline/Randomization Visit (Day 1)]{.underline}**

At the Baseline/Randomization visit, the following procedures will be performed:

Confirmation of continued eligibility will be performed, including review of all inclusion and exclusion criteria. Any screening laboratory values that are outside the acceptable range may be repeated. Any changes in medical status or concomitant medications since the Screening visit will be documented.

Eligible subjects will be randomized in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to one of the four treatment arms using the IRT system. Randomization will be stratified by fibrosis stage (F2 vs. F3) and presence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (yes vs. no).

Baseline assessments will be performed, including: complete physical examination, vital signs, weight, and 12-lead ECG. Baseline laboratory assessments (CBC with differential, CMP, lipid panel, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, amylase, lipase, INR) will be obtained if not performed within 14 days prior to Day 1. Baseline PK sample (pre-dose) and biomarker samples will be collected.

If the qualifying liver biopsy was obtained more than 4 weeks prior to Day 1, a fresh baseline liver biopsy will be performed. If the qualifying biopsy was obtained within 4 weeks of Day 1, that biopsy will serve as the baseline biopsy.

The first dose of study drug will be administered at the site under the direct supervision of trained site staff. Subjects will receive instruction on proper self-injection technique, including preparation of the injection site, handling of the prefilled syringe, administration of the injection, and proper disposal of used syringes. Subjects must demonstrate competency in self-injection before being discharged from the site. Study drug for home administration will be dispensed. Concomitant medications will be reviewed and documented.

**[6.4 Treatment Period Visits]{.underline}**

During the 52-week Treatment Period, subjects will return to the study site for scheduled visits at Weeks 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, and 52. A visit window of ±5 days is permitted for all treatment period visits, except for the Week 52 visit, which should occur within ±7 days of the scheduled date.

At each treatment period visit, the following assessments will be performed as indicated in the Schedule of Assessments (Table 4): targeted physical examination (or full physical examination at Week 52); vital signs; weight and BMI; clinical laboratory assessments as specified; adverse event assessment; concomitant medication review; and assessment of study drug compliance (review of subject injection diary, used and unused syringe count). Study drug will be dispensed at applicable visits.

PK blood samples will be collected at the Day 1, Week 4, Week 12, Week 24, and Week 52 visits as indicated in the Schedule of Assessments. At Weeks 4, 12, 24, and 52, both pre-dose (trough) and post-dose samples will be collected per the PK sampling schedule defined in the PK Manual.

FibroScan (transient elastography) will be performed at Week 24 and Week 52. A 12-lead ECG will be performed at Weeks 4, 12, 24, and 52.

The Week 52 visit is the End of Treatment visit and is a critical visit for the primary endpoint assessment. A paired liver biopsy will be performed at Week 52. Every reasonable effort must be made to obtain the Week 52 biopsy, including for subjects who have discontinued study drug early but remain in the study. The Week 52 visit will also include a complete physical examination, all protocol-specified laboratory assessments, FibroScan, 12-lead ECG, PK blood samples, and biomarker samples.

**[6.5 Post-Treatment Follow-Up Visits]{.underline}**

Following the completion of the Treatment Period, subjects will return for three post-treatment follow-up visits at Weeks 56, 60, and 64 (corresponding to 4, 8, and 12 weeks after the last dose of study drug, respectively). The purpose of the follow-up period is to assess the durability of treatment effects, monitor for delayed adverse events, and collect safety data following cessation of study drug.

At each follow-up visit, the following assessments will be performed: targeted physical examination (full physical examination at Week 64); vital signs; weight and BMI; clinical laboratory assessments as specified in the Schedule of Assessments; adverse event assessment; and concomitant medication review. A 12-lead ECG will be performed at the Week 64 (End of Study) visit.

The Week 64 visit is the End of Study visit. All outstanding queries will be resolved, and the subject\'s study participation will be formally concluded. Subjects who experience ongoing adverse events at the time of the End of Study visit will continue to be followed until resolution, stabilization, or until a determination is made that the event is unlikely to resolve.

**[SECTION 7: PHARMACOKINETIC ASSESSMENTS]{.underline}**

Pharmacokinetic (PK) blood samples will be collected at the following time points to characterize the PK profile of PTX-4820 and to support dose-response and exposure-response analyses:

> • **Day 1 (Baseline):** Pre-dose sample (trough) collected prior to the first dose of study drug.
>
> • **Week 4:** Pre-dose (trough) sample collected immediately prior to dosing, and post-dose samples collected at approximately 2, 4, 8, and 24 hours after dosing (subjects at selected PK-intensive sites) or pre-dose and 4-hour post-dose samples (all other sites). By Week 4, all subjects in Arms A, B, and C will have reached steady-state concentrations at their assigned dose level.
>
> • **Week 12:** Pre-dose (trough) sample and 4-hour post-dose sample.
>
> • **Week 24:** Pre-dose (trough) sample and 4-hour post-dose sample.
>
> • **Week 52:** Pre-dose (trough) sample and 4-hour post-dose sample.

At each sampling time point, approximately 4 mL of venous blood will be collected into K2-EDTA tubes. Samples will be processed to plasma by centrifugation within 60 minutes of collection, aliquoted, and stored at -70°C (±10°C) until shipment to the central bioanalytical laboratory (Greystone Bioanalytics, Inc.) on dry ice. Detailed instructions for sample collection, processing, labeling, storage, and shipping are provided in the PK Laboratory Manual.

The following PK parameters will be estimated using non-compartmental and/or population PK methods:

> • Maximum observed plasma concentration (Cmax)
>
> • Trough plasma concentration (Ctrough)
>
> • Area under the plasma concentration-time curve over the dosing interval at steady state (AUC0-tau)
>
> • Terminal elimination half-life (t½)
>
> • Apparent clearance (CL/F)
>
> • Apparent volume of distribution (Vd/F)

A population PK model will be developed using the sparse and intensive PK sampling data collected across all dose levels. Covariates of interest for the population PK model will include body weight, BMI, age, sex, renal function, hepatic function, and diabetes status. Details of the PK analysis methods will be provided in a separate PK Analysis Plan, which will be finalized prior to database lock.

**[SECTION 8: EFFICACY ASSESSMENTS]{.underline}**

**[8.1 Liver Biopsy and Histological Assessment]{.underline}**

Paired liver biopsies constitute the cornerstone of the efficacy evaluation in this study. A qualifying liver biopsy at baseline and a repeat liver biopsy at Week 52 are required for assessment of the primary endpoint and several key secondary endpoints.

**Biopsy Technique.** Liver biopsies will be performed as percutaneous needle biopsies using an 18-gauge or 16-gauge biopsy needle under ultrasound guidance. Biopsies should be obtained from the right lobe of the liver. The minimum acceptable biopsy specimen length is 20 mm, and the minimum number of portal tracts for an evaluable specimen is 11. Biopsies that do not meet these quality thresholds will be considered inadequate, and the investigator should consider obtaining an additional specimen. The biopsy procedure will be performed by experienced operators (hepatologists, interventional radiologists, or other qualified physicians) in accordance with each site\'s standard biopsy protocol.

**Specimen Processing.** Following collection, liver biopsy specimens will be immediately placed in 10% neutral buffered formalin and processed for paraffin embedding per standard histological procedures. From each paraffin block, the following stained slides will be prepared: hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stain and Masson\'s trichrome stain. Additional unstained slides will be prepared and archived for potential future analyses. All slides will be shipped to the central pathology reading facility per instructions provided in the Pathology Manual.

**Centralized Histological Assessment.** All liver biopsy specimens will be scored by a central pathologist experienced in NASH histological assessment using the NASH Clinical Research Network (NASH CRN) scoring system. The central pathologist will be blinded to treatment assignment, visit sequence, and clinical data. The central pathologist will score each specimen for the following parameters:

> • **NAFLD Activity Score (NAS):** Sum of individual scores for steatosis (0--3), lobular inflammation (0--3), and hepatocyte ballooning (0--2), for a total NAS range of 0--8.
>
> • **Fibrosis Stage:** Scored from F0 (no fibrosis) to F4 (cirrhosis), per the NASH CRN fibrosis staging system.

The detailed scoring criteria for each NAS component and fibrosis stage are provided in Appendix B. The central pathologist will also provide an overall assessment of whether NASH is present, absent, or borderline, based on a pattern-recognition approach.

Quality assurance measures for histological assessment will include periodic calibration sessions between the central pathologist and the Sponsor\'s medical team, and a random re-reading of approximately 10% of specimens for internal quality control.

**[8.2 Non-Invasive Assessments]{.underline}**

In addition to liver biopsy, several non-invasive assessments will be used to evaluate treatment effects on liver disease and metabolic parameters:

**FibroScan (Transient Elastography).** Liver stiffness will be measured by FibroScan at Screening, Week 24, and Week 52. FibroScan measurements will be performed by trained and certified operators at each site using FibroScan 502 Touch devices with the M or XL probe (selected based on BMI per manufacturer guidelines). A valid measurement requires a minimum of 10 successful acquisitions with an interquartile range/median ratio ≤30% and a success rate ≥60%.

**Laboratory Assessments.** Serum ALT and AST levels will be measured at all treatment period visits as part of the comprehensive metabolic panel. Changes from baseline in ALT and AST are key secondary endpoints.

**Body Weight.** Body weight will be measured at every study visit using a calibrated scale, with subjects wearing light indoor clothing and no shoes. Change from baseline in body weight (absolute and percentage) is a key secondary endpoint.

**Biomarker Assessments.** The Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) score, Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4), and AST to Platelet Ratio Index (APRI) will be calculated at Screening, Week 24, and Week 52 using available laboratory data and commercially available assays for ELF components. These biomarker assessments support the exploratory objectives of the study.

**[SECTION 9: SAFETY ASSESSMENTS]{.underline}**

**[9.1 Safety Reporting]{.underline}**

**Adverse Event Definition.** An adverse event (AE) is defined as any untoward medical occurrence in a clinical study subject administered a pharmaceutical product, which does not necessarily have

e a causal relationship with the treatment. An AE can therefore be any unfavorable and unintended sign (including abnormal laboratory findings), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of the study drug, whether or not considered related to the study drug.

**Serious Adverse Event Definition.** A serious adverse event (SAE) is any AE that at any dose:

> • Results in death
>
> • Is life-threatening (defined as an event in which the subject was at risk of death at the time of the event; this does not refer to an event that hypothetically might have caused death if it were more severe)
>
> • Requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongs an existing hospitalization
>
> • Results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity
>
> • Is a congenital anomaly or birth defect
>
> • Is an important medical event that may not meet the above criteria but, based on appropriate medical judgment, may jeopardize the subject and may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the outcomes listed above

**Adverse Event Collection Period.** Adverse events will be collected from the time of the first dose of study drug (Day 1) through 12 weeks after the last dose of study drug (i.e., through the Week 64 End of Study visit). Pre-treatment events meeting the definition of an AE that occur between informed consent and the first dose of study drug will be recorded as medical history.

**Investigator Responsibilities.** The investigator is responsible for detecting, documenting, and reporting all AEs and SAEs that occur during the AE collection period. All AEs, regardless of severity or relationship to study drug, will be recorded in the eCRF. For each AE, the investigator will record: the event term (using standard medical terminology), onset date, resolution date (or notation that the event is ongoing), severity grade (per CTCAE v5.0), seriousness criteria (if applicable), relationship to study drug (related or not related, as assessed by the investigator), action taken with respect to study drug, and outcome.

**SAE Reporting.** All SAEs must be reported by the investigator to the Sponsor (via the Trident CRO safety reporting system) within 48 hours of the investigator becoming aware of the event. An initial SAE report form must be completed and transmitted within this timeframe, with follow-up information provided as it becomes available.

**Sponsor Reporting to Regulatory Authorities.** The Sponsor will report safety events to regulatory authorities as required by applicable law. The Sponsor\'s pharmacovigilance department will evaluate all reported SAEs for expectedness and causality to determine applicable reporting obligations.

**Causality Assessment.** The investigator will assess the causal relationship between each AE and the study drug using the following categories:

> • **Not related:** There is not a reasonable possibility that the study drug caused the AE, based on temporal relationship, clinical judgment, and known pharmacology.
>
> • **Related:** There is a reasonable possibility that the study drug caused the AE.

**Severity Grading.** The severity of AEs will be graded using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE), Version 5.0. For AEs not specifically listed in the CTCAE, the following general grading scale will be used: Grade 1 (Mild), Grade 2 (Moderate), Grade 3 (Severe), Grade 4 (Life-threatening), Grade 5 (Death).

**Follow-Up.** All AEs will be followed until resolution, stabilization, return to baseline, or until a determination is made that the event is chronic or that further follow-up is unlikely to yield additional information. SAEs that are ongoing at the time of the End of Study visit will continue to be followed and reported until resolution or stabilization.

**[9.2 Adverse Events of Special Interest]{.underline}**

The following categories of events have been identified as adverse events of special interest (AESIs) for this study and will be subject to enhanced monitoring, reporting, and evaluation:

> 1\. **Drug-Induced Liver Injury (DILI):** Any suspected case of DILI, including cases meeting Hy\'s Law criteria (ALT or AST \>3× ULN AND total bilirubin \>2× ULN in the absence of other identifiable causes, including cholestasis as indicated by ALP \>2× ULN). All potential Hy\'s Law cases will be subject to a comprehensive causality evaluation per the Sponsor\'s DILI Assessment Protocol.
>
> 2\. **Pancreatitis:** Any case of suspected acute or chronic pancreatitis, including events characterized by severe abdominal pain with amylase and/or lipase elevations \>3× ULN consistent with a diagnosis of pancreatitis.
>
> 3\. **Thyroid Neoplasms:** Any report of thyroid nodules, thyroid carcinoma (including medullary thyroid carcinoma), or C-cell hyperplasia.
>
> 4\. **Severe Gastrointestinal Events:** Any gastrointestinal AE of CTCAE Grade 3 or higher, including severe nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, or gastroparesis.
>
> 5\. **Hepatic Decompensation Events:** Any event of variceal bleeding, new-onset or worsening ascites requiring treatment (diuretics, paracentesis), hepatic encephalopathy (any grade), or hepatorenal syndrome.
>
> 6\. **Injection Site Reactions:** Any injection site reaction of CTCAE Grade 2 or higher, or any injection site reaction resulting in study drug discontinuation.
>
> 7\. **Hypoglycemia:** Any event of symptomatic hypoglycemia (blood glucose \<54 mg/dL \[\<3.0 mmol/L\]) or severe hypoglycemia requiring assistance of another person, particularly in subjects with type 2 diabetes on concomitant antidiabetic medications.

All AESIs, regardless of seriousness, will be reported to the Sponsor within 48 hours of investigator awareness using the AESI reporting form, and will be subject to expedited medical review by the Sponsor\'s Medical Monitor.

**[9.3 Clinical Laboratory Safety Assessments]{.underline}**

Safety laboratory assessments will be performed at visits indicated in the Schedule of Assessments (Table 4). All protocol-specified laboratory assessments will be performed by the central laboratory (Greystone Bioanalytics, Inc.), with the exception of point-of-care tests that may be permitted for immediate safety management at the investigator\'s discretion.

The following standard safety laboratory tests will be performed:

> • **Hematology:** CBC with differential (white blood cells, red blood cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit, platelets, neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils)
>
> • **Chemistry / Liver Function:** Comprehensive metabolic panel including ALT, AST, ALP, total bilirubin, direct bilirubin, albumin, total protein, BUN, creatinine (with eGFR calculation), sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate, calcium, glucose; INR
>
> • **Pancreatic Enzymes:** Amylase, lipase
>
> • **Lipid Panel:** Total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides
>
> • **Thyroid Function:** TSH, free T4 (at Screening, Week 24, Week 52)
>
> • **Glycemic Control:** HbA1c (at Screening, Week 24, Week 52); fasting glucose and fasting insulin (at Screening, Day 1, Week 12, Week 24, Week 52)
>
> • **Urinalysis:** Specific gravity, pH, protein, glucose, ketones, blood, leukocyte esterase

Laboratory reference ranges will be provided by the central laboratory. All laboratory values will be reviewed by the investigator, and clinically significant abnormalities will be documented as adverse events if they meet the definition of an AE as described in Section 9.1.

**[9.4 Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB)]{.underline}**

An independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) may be convened at the Sponsor\'s discretion to review accumulating safety data during the conduct of this study. If convened, the DSMB will consist of independent physicians and a statistician who are not otherwise involved in the conduct of the study. The DSMB charter, including membership, meeting schedule, and operating procedures, will be finalized prior to the first DSMB meeting.

If the DSMB is convened, its primary responsibilities will include periodic review of unblinded safety data, including the incidence and severity of adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse events of special interest, and any emerging safety signals. The DSMB may make recommendations to the Sponsor regarding the continuation, modification, or termination of the study based on its review of safety data. The Sponsor will retain ultimate responsibility for decisions regarding the conduct of the study.

**[9.5 Stopping Rules]{.underline}**

**9.5.1 Individual Subject Stopping Criteria**

Study drug must be permanently discontinued for an individual subject if any of the following criteria are met:

> 1\. **ALT Elevation:** ALT \>10× ULN, confirmed on repeat testing performed within 72 hours of the initial elevated result.
>
> 2\. **Drug-Induced Liver Injury (Hy\'s Law):** ALT or AST \>3× ULN AND total bilirubin \>2× ULN (in the absence of biliary obstruction or other identified cause for the combined elevation), consistent with Hy\'s Law criteria.
>
> 3\. **Anaphylaxis or Severe Hypersensitivity:** Occurrence of anaphylaxis or a severe systemic hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., angioedema, severe urticaria with hemodynamic compromise) attributed to the study drug.
>
> 4\. **Pregnancy:** If a subject is found to be pregnant during the study, study drug must be immediately discontinued. The pregnancy will be reported to the Sponsor and followed to outcome.
>
> 5\. **Subject Request:** The subject requests discontinuation of study drug.
>
> 6\. **Investigator Judgment:** The investigator determines that continued study drug administration would pose an unacceptable risk to the subject\'s health or safety.

Subjects who meet any of the above criteria for permanent discontinuation of study drug will be encouraged to remain in the study for all remaining scheduled visits and the Week 52 liver biopsy, if they are willing. The reason for study drug discontinuation will be recorded in the eCRF, and all such subjects will be included in the safety analyses.

In addition, the investigator should consider temporary interruption of study drug (with Medical Monitor consultation) for the following situations:

> • ALT \>5× ULN but ≤10× ULN: Repeat testing within 48--72 hours; if confirmed, hold study drug and repeat weekly until ALT \<3× ULN, then resume at the same dose with Medical Monitor approval.
>
> • Severe or persistent gastrointestinal symptoms (Grade 3 or higher nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea) lasting \>7 days despite supportive management: Hold study drug; may resume at a reduced dose level (one step down) with Medical Monitor approval.

**[SECTION 10: STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS]{.underline}**

**[10.1 Sample Size Determination]{.underline}**

The sample size for this study was determined based on the primary comparison between the PTX-4820 30 mg arm (Arm C) and the placebo arm (Arm D) for the primary efficacy endpoint.

The following assumptions were used for the sample size calculation:

> • **Placebo response rate:** 30%. This is the expected proportion of subjects in the placebo arm who will achieve ≥1-stage improvement in liver fibrosis with no worsening of NASH at Week 52. This rate is based on published data from Phase 2 and Phase 3 studies in NASH populations with fibrosis stages F2--F3, where placebo fibrosis improvement rates have been reported in the range of 20--35%.
>
> • **Treatment response rate (30 mg arm):** 45%. This is the expected proportion of subjects in the PTX-4820 30 mg arm who will achieve the primary endpoint.
>
> • **Treatment difference:** 15 percentage points (45% minus 30%).
>
> • **Type I error rate (alpha):** 0.05, two-sided.
>
> • **Power:** 80%.
>
> • **Statistical test:** Chi-square test of proportions (or Fisher\'s exact test as appropriate).

Using these assumptions, the sample size required to detect a 15-percentage-point treatment difference with 80% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.05 is approximately 78 evaluable subjects per arm. To account for an anticipated dropout rate of approximately 15% (including subjects who do not complete the Week 52 liver biopsy), the number of subjects to be randomized per arm is 78 / 0.85 ≈ 92, rounded to 90 subjects per arm.

**Table 5: Sample Size Calculation Summary**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Parameter**                       **Value**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Placebo response rate               30%

  Treatment response rate (30 mg)     45%

  Treatment difference                15 percentage points

  Alpha (two-sided)                   0.05

  Power                               80%

  Evaluable N per arm                 78

  Dropout allowance                   15%

  Randomized N per arm                90

  Total randomized N                  360
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The study includes three active dose arms (5 mg, 15 mg, 30 mg) and one placebo arm, randomized 1:1:1:1, providing 90 subjects per arm and a total of 360 subjects. This design supports both the primary efficacy comparison (30 mg vs. placebo) and secondary dose-response evaluations across all three dose levels.

**[10.2 Analysis Populations]{.underline}**

The following analysis populations will be defined for this study:

**Table 6: Analysis Populations**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Population**                    **Definition**                                                                                                                                                                                                    **Primary Use**
  --------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Intent-to-Treat (ITT)             All randomized subjects who receive at least one dose of study drug, analyzed according to randomized treatment assignment                                                                                        Sensitivity analysis for efficacy

  Modified Intent-to-Treat (mITT)   All ITT subjects who have a qualifying baseline liver biopsy and at least one post-baseline liver biopsy (Week 52), analyzed according to randomized treatment assignment                                         Primary efficacy analysis

  Per-Protocol (PP)                 All mITT subjects who complete at least 80% of scheduled study drug doses, have both baseline and Week 52 biopsies, and do not have major protocol deviations that could affect the primary endpoint assessment   Sensitivity analysis for efficacy

  Safety Population                 All subjects who receive at least one dose of study drug, analyzed according to actual treatment received                                                                                                         Safety analyses

  PK Population                     All subjects with at least one evaluable PK sample                                                                                                                                                                PK analyses
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The primary efficacy analysis will be performed on the mITT population. Sensitivity analyses will be performed on the ITT and PP populations. Safety analyses will be performed on the Safety Population. PK analyses will be performed on the PK Population.

**[10.3 Interim Analysis]{.underline}**

A single planned interim efficacy analysis will be performed when all enrolled subjects have completed the Week 26 visit (i.e., at Week 26 of the last enrolled subject). The interim analysis will compare the primary endpoint across treatment arms using the mITT population available at that time.

An O\'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function will be used to control the overall Type I error rate across the interim and final analyses. The nominal significance level at the interim analysis will be determined based on the information fraction at the time of the analysis. Specifically, the O\'Brien-Fleming boundary will be applied to maintain the overall two-sided alpha at 0.05 for the primary comparison (PTX-4820 30 mg vs. placebo). If the interim analysis is performed at an information fraction of approximately 50%, the nominal alpha at the interim analysis is expected to be approximately 0.003.

The interim analysis will be conducted by an independent statistical group that is not involved in the day-to-day conduct of the study. Interim analysis results will be shared only with the DSMB (if convened) and a limited number of authorized Sponsor personnel, as specified in the DSMB charter. The study team, investigators, and subjects will remain blinded to interim analysis results.

Details of the interim analysis methodology, decision criteria, and alpha-spending function specifications will be provided in the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP), which will be finalized prior to database lock for the interim analysis.

**[10.4 Primary Efficacy Analysis]{.underline}**

The primary efficacy analysis will compare the proportion of subjects achieving ≥1-stage improvement in fibrosis with no worsening of NASH at Week 52 between each PTX-4820 dose group and the placebo group, using the mITT population.

The primary statistical test will be the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) test, stratified by the randomization stratification factors (fibrosis stage: F2 vs. F3; type 2 diabetes: yes vs. no). The primary comparison will be PTX-4820 30 mg versus placebo. Pairwise comparisons of the 5 mg and 15 mg arms versus placebo will be performed as secondary comparisons.

Multiplicity across dose groups will be controlled using the Hochberg step-up procedure. Under this approach, if the highest p-value among the three dose-versus-placebo comparisons is ≤0.05, all three comparisons are declared significant. If not, the two remaining lower p-values are tested using a Hochberg adjustment, and so forth.

The following sensitivity analyses are planned for the primary endpoint:

> • Logistic regression model with treatment, fibrosis stage, diabetes status, and baseline NAS as covariates
>
> • ITT analysis using multiple imputation for subjects with missing Week 52 biopsies, with missing data imputed under the assumption that the outcome is missing at random (MAR)
>
> • Tipping point analysis to evaluate the robustness of results under various assumptions about missing data (missing not at random scenarios)
>
> • Per-Protocol population analysis

**[10.5 Secondary Efficacy Analyses]{.underline}**

Key secondary endpoints will be analyzed hierarchically to control the familywise Type I error rate. The analysis of each secondary endpoint will proceed in the order specified in Section 3.4.2 only if the preceding endpoint achieves statistical significance.

The proportion of subjects achieving NASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis and the proportion achieving ≥2-point reduction in NAS will be analyzed similarly to the primary endpoint, using the CMH test stratified by fibrosis stage and diabetes status.

Continuous secondary endpoints (change from baseline in ALT, AST, liver stiffness, and body weight) will be analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM) with treatment, visit, treatment-by-visit interaction as fixed effects, baseline value as a covariate, and randomization stratification factors. An unstructured covariance matrix will be used for within-subject correlation.

Dose-response relationships will be explored using both graphical methods and formal dose-response modeling, including Emax and linear dose-response models fitted to the proportion of responders and the change from baseline in continuous endpoints across the three active dose levels and placebo.

**[10.6 Safety Analyses]{.underline}**

Safety analyses will be descriptive and performed on the Safety Population. The incidence of AEs, SAEs, AESIs, and AEs leading to discontinuation will be summarized by treatment arm, system organ class, and preferred term (MedDRA coding). Exposure-adjusted incidence rates (events per 100 patient-years) will be calculated for key safety endpoints.

Shift tables will be prepared for selected laboratory parameters, displaying the shift from baseline category (normal, low, high) to worst post-baseline category. For continuous laboratory parameters and vital signs, summary statistics (mean, median, standard deviation, range) and change from baseline will be tabulated by treatment arm and visit. Kaplan-Meier estimates will be generated for time to first AE and time to discontinuation due to AE by treatment arm.

ECG parameters, including the QTcF interval, will be summarized by treatment arm and visit. The proportion of subjects with QTcF \>450 ms, \>480 ms, and \>500 ms, as well as the proportion with QTcF change from baseline \>30 ms and \>60 ms, will be reported.

**[11.2 Institutional Review Board / Ethics Committee]{.underline}**

This protocol and the informed consent form must be reviewed and approved by an Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Ethics Committee (EC) before enrollment begins at any investigational site. The Sponsor will work with each Canadian site to identify the appropriate REB and ensure that all required approvals are in place prior to site activation.

The IRB/EC will receive the following for review and approval: the protocol and any amendments; the informed consent form and any revisions; the Investigator\'s Brochure and any updates; relevant recruitment materials; and any other documents required by the IRB/EC.

**[11.3 Protection of Vulnerable Populations]{.underline}**

This study enrolls only adults aged 18 to 75 years. No pediatric subjects (individuals under 18 years of age) will be enrolled. The exclusion of pediatric subjects is appropriate given the early stage of clinical development and the absence of established pediatric dosing information for PTX-4820.

No specific provisions are included for the enrollment or protection of other categories of vulnerable populations, including prisoners, individuals who are cognitively impaired, or economically or educationally disadvantaged persons. The investigator is responsible for ensuring that each subject is capable of understanding the informed consent process and providing voluntary informed consent.

**[11.4 Subject Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Subject confidentiality will be maintained throughout the study. Each subject will be assigned a unique subject identification number at the time of enrollment, which will be used in lieu of personal identifiers (name, date of birth, medical record number) in the study database, case report forms, and all study-related data transmissions.

Source documents containing personal identifiers will be maintained securely at each investigational site in accordance with the site\'s institutional policies for the protection of medical records. Access to source documents will be limited to authorized study personnel, clinical monitors, auditors, and regulatory inspectors.

Data transferred from the investigational sites to the Sponsor and/or CRO will be transmitted in a de-identified format using secure, encrypted electronic systems. Personal identifiers will not be transmitted to the Sponsor except as required for individual safety reports.

The Sponsor, its agents, regulatory authorities (including the FDA), and the IRB/EC may require direct access to source documents and medical records for the purpose of monitoring, auditing, or inspecting the study. Subject consent for such access is obtained as part of the informed consent process.

Compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and applicable state and local privacy laws will be maintained for all U.S. sites. A HIPAA authorization form will be included with the informed consent documents for U.S. sites as required.

**[SECTION 12: DATA MANAGEMENT AND QUALITY ASSURANCE]{.underline}**

**[12.1 Electronic Data Capture]{.underline}**

All clinical study data will be captured electronically using TrialVault, Trident Clinical Research Organization\'s proprietary electronic data capture (EDC) system. TrialVault is a web-based system accessible via standard internet browsers with appropriate security credentials.

Authorized site personnel (investigators, study coordinators, and other delegated staff as listed on the delegation of authority log) will enter data from source documents into electronic case report forms (eCRFs) within the TrialVault system. Data entry should be performed in a timely manner following each subject visit, generally within 5 business days for routine visits and within 24 hours for serious adverse events.

TrialVault includes built-in programmatic edit checks, range checks, and cross-field consistency checks designed to promote data quality and integrity at the time of data entry. When entered data trigger an edit check, the system will generate a query that is presented to the site user for review and resolution. In addition to programmatic checks, manual data queries may be generated by clinical data managers during periodic data review. All queries will be managed and resolved within the TrialVault system. Sites will respond to data queries in a timely manner, generally within 5 business days of query generation.

TrialVault provides role-based user access, with each user assigned a unique login identifier and password. User access permissions are configured based on the user\'s role (e.g., investigator, study coordinator, data manager, monitor) to ensure that users have access only to the functions and data appropriate to their responsibilities. All users will receive training on the TrialVault system prior to being granted access.

Data management activities, including data entry guidelines, query management procedures, coding conventions (MedDRA for adverse events, WHO Drug Dictionary for medications), and data review processes, will be described in the Data Management Plan, which will be finalized prior to the first subject enrollment.

**[12.2 Data Quality and Monitoring]{.underline}**

A risk-based monitoring approach will be employed for this study, in accordance with the principles outlined in ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3. The monitoring strategy will incorporate a combination of on-site monitoring, remote/centralized data monitoring, and statistical data surveillance to ensure subject safety, data integrity, and protocol compliance.

**On-Site Monitoring.** Clinical Research Associates (CRAs) from Trident Clinical Research Organization will perform on-site monitoring visits throughout the study, including:

> • **Site Initiation Visits (SIVs):** Conducted prior to the first subject enrollment at each site to verify site readiness, review protocol requirements, train site staff, and confirm regulatory document completeness.
>
> • **Routine Monitoring Visits:** Conducted at approximately monthly intervals during active enrollment and every 6--8 weeks during the treatment period. Monitoring activities include: source data verification (SDV) for critical data elements (primary endpoint data, serious adverse events, key eligibility criteria, informed consent documentation); review of study drug accountability; verification of essential regulatory documents; and identification and resolution of protocol deviations.
>
> • **Close-Out Visits:** Conducted at each site following completion of all study activities to reconcile study drug accountability, resolve outstanding data queries, archive essential documents, and formally close the site.

**Centralized Monitoring.** In addition to on-site monitoring, centralized data monitoring will be conducted by the Trident data management and biostatistics teams. Centralized monitoring activities include tracking key risk indicators (KRIs) such as enrollment rates, data entry timeliness, query resolution rates, protocol deviation rates, AE reporting rates, and other metrics identified in the Monitoring Plan. Statistical data monitoring will include central review of data distributions and patterns to identify potential data anomalies or fraud indicators.

**[12.3 Data Lock and Archiving]{.underline}**

Upon completion of all data entry, query resolution, medical coding, and data review activities, the database will be formally locked in accordance with the procedures described in the Data Management Plan. Prior to database lock, the Sponsor, CRO, and biostatistician will conduct a data review meeting to confirm that all outstanding issues have been resolved and that the database is ready for lock and analysis.

The database lock will occur separately for the interim analysis (if applicable) and the final analysis. For the interim analysis, a snapshot of the database will be taken and provided to the independent statistical group for analysis, while data entry and cleaning will continue for ongoing subjects.

Archiving of essential study documents will be performed in accordance with ICH E6(R2) and applicable regulatory requirements. The investigator and Sponsor will retain essential documents for at least 2 years after the last approval of a marketing application in an ICH region, or at least 2 years after formal discontinuation of clinical development of PTX-4820, whichever is later. Sites will be notified in writing before any documents may be destroyed.

**[SECTION 13: REGULATORY AND ADMINISTRATIVE CONSIDERATIONS]{.underline}**

**[13.1 Regulatory Submissions]{.underline}**

This study will be conducted under an Investigational New Drug (IND) application submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), Division of Hepatology and Nutrition (DHN). The IND application is targeted for submission on or around September 15, 2025.

Following IND submission, the Sponsor will observe the 30-day FDA safety review period before initiating enrollment at any U.S. investigational site. If the FDA places the IND on clinical hold, enrollment will not proceed until the clinical hold is lifted. If the FDA does not communicate any objections within the 30-day review period, the study may proceed.

All protocol amendments, including both substantial and administrative amendments, will be submitted to the FDA as IND amendments in accordance with 21 CFR 312.30. Substantial amendments (those affecting subject safety, study scope, study design, or the scientific quality of the study) will be submitted prior to implementation and will require IRB/EC approval before implementation at investigational sites.

Annual reports will be submitted to the FDA in accordance with 21 CFR 312.33, summarizing the progress of the investigation, safety information, and any relevant changes to the study. Annual reports will be submitted within 60 days of the anniversary date of the IND.

The Sponsor will maintain the IND in active status throughout the conduct of the study and will comply with all applicable FDA requirements for IND sponsors, including record-keeping, reporting, and inspection obligations.

**[13.2 Protocol Amendments]{.underline}**

All protocol amendments must be approved by the Sponsor\'s Chief Medical Officer (Dr. Rajiv Anand) or designee prior to implementation. The Sponsor will classify each amendment as substantial or non-substantial based on the nature of the changes.

Substantial amendments --- those that affect subject safety, eligibility criteria, study conduct, study endpoints, or the scientific integrity of the study --- will be submitted to the IRB/EC and applicable regulatory authorities for review and approval prior to implementation at any investigational site. Non-substantial amendments (e.g., administrative corrections, clarifications that do not affect study conduct) will be documented, filed with the IRB/EC as required by the IRB\'s policies, and implemented upon Sponsor approval.

All amendments will be tracked in the protocol amendment history log, which will document the amendment number, date, description of changes, and rationale for each amendment.

**[13.3 Study Committees]{.underline}**

**Steering Committee.** A Steering Committee will provide scientific and operational oversight of the study. The Steering Committee will be chaired by the Sponsor\'s Chief Medical Officer (Dr. Rajiv Anand) and will include Principal Investigators from selected high-enrolling sites, the Trident Project Lead (Dr. Caroline Xu), and Sponsor representatives from clinical development, biostatistics, and regulatory affairs. The Steering Committee will meet approximately quarterly (or more frequently as needed) to review enrollment progress, operational issues, and emerging data trends.

**Endpoint Adjudication Committee.** An independent Endpoint Adjudication Committee (EAC) will be established to adjudicate key clinical events, including hepatic decompensation events and cardiovascular events. The EAC will consist of independent hepatologists and cardiologists who are not otherwise involved in the study. The EAC charter will define the committee membership, operating procedures, event definitions, and adjudication criteria. The EAC will operate in a blinded manner with respect to treatment assignment.

**Data Safety Monitoring Board.** The establishment and operation of the DSMB are described in Section 9.4.

**[13.4 Insurance and Compensation]{.underline}**

Clinical trial insurance for this study has been obtained through Ashford Re Insurance Ltd., providing coverage for claims arising from study-related injuries to subjects enrolled in the study. The insurance policy covers all investigational sites and is maintained in compliance with local regulatory and institutional requirements.

Subjects will be compensated for their time, inconvenience, and travel expenses associated with study participation. Compensation will be provided per a payment schedule approved by the IRB, at a rate of up to \$150 per completed study visit. Total maximum compensation for a subject who completes all 17 scheduled study visits (from Day 1 through the Week 64 End of Study visit) is approximately \$2,550.

Payment will be prorated based on the number of visits completed. Subjects who withdraw from the study will receive compensation for visits completed up to the date of withdrawal. Payment schedules will comply with IRB guidelines and will not be coercive or constitute undue inducement for participation.

**[13.5 Publication Policy]{.underline}**

The Sponsor is committed to the timely publication and dissemination of study results, regardless of outcome. Results of this study will be submitted for publication in peer-reviewed medical or scientific journals and/or presented at relevant scientific conferences.

Authorship will be determined in accordance with the criteria established by the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE). Investigators and other contributors who meet the ICMJE criteria for authorship will be invited to serve as authors. Professional medical writers may assist with manuscript preparation, and their contributions will be acknowledged in accordance with ICMJE guidelines.

Pinnacle Therapeutics retains the right to review any manuscripts, abstracts, or presentations prior to submission for publication to ensure that confidential or proprietary information is not inadvertently disclosed. The Sponsor will complete its review within 60 days of receipt. The Sponsor may not unreasonably withhold consent for publication.

**[13.6 Clinical Trial Registration]{.underline}**

This study will be registered on ClinicalTrials.gov prior to enrollment of the first subject, in compliance with the requirements of Section 801 of the Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act of 2007 (FDAAA 801) and the implementing regulations at 42 CFR Part 11. The study registry record will include all required data elements, including the protocol summary, eligibility criteria, study design, endpoints, and contact information.

The study registry will be updated with summary results data within 12 months of the primary completion date, as required by applicable law and regulations.

**Section A1: Introduction and Purpose**

You are being asked to take part in a research study. Before you decide whether to participate, it is important for you to understand why the research is being done and what it will involve. Please take time to read the following information carefully and discuss it with your doctor, family members, or others as you wish. Ask the study doctor or study staff if there is anything that is not clear or if you would like more information.

ional drug called PTX-4820 for the treatment of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), a condition in which fat builds up in the liver and causes inflammation and damage. You are being asked to participate because you have been diagnosed with NASH that has caused scarring (fibrosis) in your liver.

PTX-4820 is an investigational drug, which means it is not approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or any other regulatory authority for any use. PTX-4820 is designed to work on two specific targets in the body (called GLP-1 and GIP receptors) that may reduce fat in the liver, decrease liver inflammation, and reduce liver scarring.

This study is \"randomized,\" meaning that if you choose to participate, you will be assigned by chance (like flipping a coin) to one of four study groups. This study is also \"double-blind,\" meaning that neither you nor the study doctor will know which group you are in during the study. The four groups are:

> • Group 1: PTX-4820 at a dose of 5 mg, given as a weekly injection under the skin
>
> • Group 2: PTX-4820 at a dose of 15 mg, given as a weekly injection under the skin
>
> • Group 3: PTX-4820 at a dose of 30 mg, given as a weekly injection under the skin
>
> • Group 4: Placebo (an inactive injection that looks the same as the study drug but contains no active medication), given as a weekly injection under the skin

You have an equal chance (1 in 4) of being assigned to any of the four groups. Approximately 360 people at about 28 medical centers across the United States and Canada will take part in this study.

**Section A2: Study Procedures**

Your participation in this study will last approximately 12 months. The study includes the following types of visits and procedures:

**Screening Visit(s):** Before you can join the study, the study doctor will perform tests to determine if you are eligible. These tests may include blood and urine tests, a physical examination, vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature), an electrocardiogram (ECG, a test that measures the electrical activity of your heart), a FibroScan (a non-invasive test that measures liver stiffness), and a review of your medical history and medications. If you do not have a recent liver biopsy result that qualifies you for the study, a liver biopsy may be performed during screening.

**Treatment Period Visits:** If you are eligible and choose to participate, you will be randomized to one of the four groups and will begin receiving weekly injections of the study drug or placebo. The first injection will be given at the study site, where you will be taught how to give yourself the injections at home. You will return to the study site approximately 12 times during the treatment period for check-up visits, which will include physical examinations, vital signs, blood draws, ECGs, FibroScan, and other tests.

**Liver Biopsy:** A liver biopsy will be required at the start of the study (if not already completed during screening) and again at Week 52. A liver biopsy involves inserting a needle through your skin into your liver to obtain a small tissue sample. This will be done under local anesthesia and ultrasound guidance. You will be monitored at the site for several hours after the procedure.

**Study Drug Injection:** The study drug is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once a week. You will be taught to self-administer the injections at home using a prefilled syringe. Injections may be given in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm.

**Follow-Up Visits:** After you complete the treatment period, you will return for follow-up visits to check your health.

**Section A3: Risks and Discomforts**

As with any research study, there are risks associated with participation. The known and possible risks are described below:

**Risks of Liver Biopsy:** There is a small risk of bleeding, infection, and pain associated with the liver biopsy procedure. In rare cases, the bleeding may be serious and require medical intervention, including blood transfusion or hospitalization. There is also a very small risk of accidental puncture of other organs. Your study doctor will discuss the risks of liver biopsy with you in more detail.

**Risks of Study Drug (PTX-4820):** Because PTX-4820 is investigational, not all side effects are known. Based on the class of drugs to which PTX-4820 belongs (GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists) and preclinical studies, the following side effects are possible:

> • **Gastrointestinal side effects:** Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain, decreased appetite. These are the most commonly expected side effects and may be more frequent during the first few weeks of treatment or during dose increases.
>
> • **Injection site reactions:** Pain, redness, swelling, or itching at the injection site.
>
> • **Pancreatitis:** There is a potential risk of inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis), which can cause severe abdominal pain and may be serious. You should contact the study doctor immediately if you experience severe abdominal pain.
>
> • **Thyroid tumors:** In animal studies, drugs in this class have been associated with thyroid tumors, including a type called medullary thyroid carcinoma. It is not known whether PTX-4820 causes thyroid tumors in humans. You should not participate if you or a family member has had medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2.
>
> • **Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia):** If you have diabetes and are taking other diabetes medications (particularly sulfonylureas or insulin), PTX-4820 may increase the risk of low blood sugar.
>
> • **Other unknown risks:** Because PTX-4820 is an investigational drug, there may be risks that are not yet known.

**Risks of Blood Draws:** Blood draws may cause temporary bruising, discomfort, or pain at the site of the needle insertion. In rare cases, blood draws may cause infection, fainting, or lightheadedness.

**Section A4: Benefits**

There is no guarantee that you will receive any direct benefit from participating in this study. It is possible that PTX-4820 may improve your liver fibrosis, but this is not certain. If you are assigned to the placebo group, you will not receive the active study drug. The information gained from this study may help future patients with NASH.

**Section A5: Alternatives**

The alternative to participating in this study is not to participate. If you choose not to participate or if you withdraw from the study, your standard medical care will not be affected. Currently, there is no FDA-approved drug treatment specifically for NASH with liver fibrosis. Standard care for NASH includes lifestyle changes such as diet and exercise, weight loss, and management of related conditions such as diabetes, high cholesterol, and high blood pressure. You should discuss these alternatives with your personal doctor.

**Section A6: Voluntary Participation and Withdrawal**

Your participation in this study is entirely voluntary. You may refuse to participate or you may withdraw from the study at any time, for any reason, without penalty or loss of benefits to which you are otherwise entitled. Your decision will not affect your current or future medical care.

The study doctor or the Sponsor may also decide to end your participation in the study if it is determined to be in your best interest, if you do not follow the study rules, or for other study-related reasons. If you decide to withdraw or if your participation is ended, the study doctor will discuss with you any follow-up care that may be needed.

**Section A7: Costs and Payments**

There will be no charge to you for the study drug, study-related medical procedures, or study visits. The study drug and all protocol-required tests and procedures will be provided at no cost to you.

You will be compensated for your time and travel expenses associated with study visits. You will receive up to \$150 for each completed study visit. If you complete all scheduled study visits, your total compensation will be approximately \$2,550.
